newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: P&O says damaged Sydney crane written off.
newsitem.headline: P&O says damaged Sydney crane written off.

text.p: P&O Ports, a unit of The Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co Plc, said on Tuesday that its damaged crane at Sydney's White Bay cargo terminal was a write-off and it would probably lease a replacement crane.
The company said the crane was damaged on April 13 when it was struck by the ro-ro vessel Toba, owned by Norway's Wilhelmsen Lines.
At the time, it said a replacement crane would cost about A$10 million.

P&O said the damaged crane had just been upgraded at a cost of A$1 million and it would take up to four weeks to remove the wreckage, during which time the company would investigate leasing a replacement crane.
"We're very confident of finding ways of continuing to provide good service, but clearly there will be some impact in the short term," P&O state stevedoring manager Dean Wells said.
